The Q3 identification labels have construct-validity problems. A modified logo or flag can still reasonably be identified by its source, and unequal central circles can still exhibit the Ebbinghaus illusion. Automatically assigning 'No' to these cases conflates recognizing identity with detecting an alteration. The headline metrics are misleadingly described. The in-image text experiment lacks matched blank-header and unrelated-text controls. Extending the canvas can change effective image scaling or attention allocation, so the accuracy decrease does not uniquely establish semantic priming. Conclusions about the ineffectiveness of reasoning are also based on comparisons between different models rather than controlled reasoning-budget experiments.

Validation and statistical reporting are inadequate. There is no measured human accuracy or annotator agreement to substantiate image clarity and label reliability.
